post.description:
For an employee to be successfully added to Definitiv via an integration, there are minimum data sets that need to be provided for the following scenarios:
  1. Create an employee
  2. Pay an employee
This endpoint creates a new employee using the provided data in the newEmployee parameter. The new employee is returned in the response if the creation is successful. Otherwise, a 400 Bad Request status is returned along with validation errors in the response body.

Creating an Employee and the Minimum Data Required for Payroll

In order to pay an employee there is a minimum set of data you will need to setup:
  1. Pay Calendar - A company may have multiple pay calendars, e.g. monthly and fortnightly. It is important for the right pay calendar to be assigned to an employee so that they can be included in a scheduled pay run. Endpoint documentation
  2. Department Assignments - A department is a cost centre required to be assigned on a master record for an employee to be paid. An employee can be assigned to multiple departments, but they must always have a primary or default department. Endpoint Documentation
  3. Location Assignments - A location is a cost centre required to be assigned on a master record for an employee to be paid. Most commonly it is used to indicate the state or territory an employee is based for payroll tax, public holiday and long service leave purposes. However, it can also be used for additional reasons and employees can be assigned to towns, suburbs or regions within a state or territory. An employee can be assigned to multiple locations, but they must always have a primary or default location. A location assigned to an employee must match a value from the global Location list that can be found under Admin > Structure > Locations within the front UI. Endpoint documentation
  4. Project Assignments - A project is a cost centre required to be assigned on a master record for an employee to be paid. An employee can be assigned to multiple projects, but they must always have a primary or default project. A project is the main cost centre within Definitiv and has additional attributes compared to other cost centres types. For example, a project can define the approval workflow and what employees based on their role, location or department can work on it. Endpoint documentation
  5. Role Assignments - A role is an item required to be assigned on a master record for an employee to be paid. An employee can be assigned to multiple roles, but they must always have a primary or default role. For example, an employee may be a full-time teacher (primary role) and a casual swimming coach (additional role). As roles can have different payment conditions, e.g. hourly rates, these may need to be defined when assigning a role. A role assigned to an employee must match a value from the global role list that can be found under Admin > Structure > Roles within the front UI. Endpoint documentation
  6. Tax Declaration - Tax File Number (TFN) declarations must be completed for an employee to be included within a pay run. Endpoint documentation
  7. Bank Details - For an employee to be included in a pay run and to be paid, they must have at least one bank account on their master record. Multiple bank accounts and payment splits can be assigned to an employee. If multiple bank accounts exist for an employee, the last one must be set as “Remainder” to ensure any surplus funds once all the other rules for preceding bank accounts have been processed. Endpoint documentation
  8. Superannuation Details - The superannuation details including the superannuation fund, contribution type and amount must be entered for the employee to ensure a company meets its minimum superannuation guarantee requirements. Endpoint documentation
  9. Leave Policies - Leave Policies must be assigned to the employee to correctly calculate leave accruals. Important Note: Casuals may not require annual or personal leave accruals, however, they may need a long service leave policy applied. You can also assign a leave policy with no accruals to an employee, if applicable. Endpoint documentation

Other important considerations

Time and Attendance

Depending on an employee’s employment type and the company’s preference for rostering and capturing timesheets, time and attendance data must be provided if an employee is to be paid for the hours they have worked. Definitiv does have in-built workforce management capability, or time and attendance data can be sent via API. Below is information to help determine what needs to be considered as part of an integration:
  1. Work schedules - These set-and-forget rosters are common for salaried employees or employees working repetitive work patterns. For example, a Monday through Friday or a repetitive nine days on, five days off schedule. Important Note: Casual employees will generally not have a Work Schedule, as they do not work a recurring pattern. Endpoint documentation
  2. Rostering - Rosters are created in advance and can be updated on-the-go. They are commonly used to manage a casual workforce or resource capacity for projects or jobs. Endpoint documentation
  3. Time clock events - If another system is being used to clock on and off, these events can be sent to Definitiv. This is common if the company is using its own time clock hardware but would like the timesheet approval process to be within Definitiv. Sending time clock events will also allow managers and the company to remain up to date on an employee’s movements.
  4. Timesheets - With Definitiv, an employee can be paid based on their work schedule, roster, submitted and approved timesheet or a combination of both depending on a company’s operations. If the timesheet process is being managed in another system, you may only want to send approved timesheets in Definitiv. Endpoint documentation
  5. Leave - If the leave process is being managed in another system, you may only want to send approved leave requests. While not covered in this section, if leave is being managed in another system, you may want to also retrieve leave balances from Definitiv. Endpoint documentation

Non time and attendance payments or deductions

  1. Additions and deductions - If an employee is to receive a recurring payment, allowance or deduction that is not driven by the hours they worked, a company can automate these through the payroll by setting them up on the employee master record, e.g. child support, novated lease and salary sacrifice deductions. Endpoint documentation
  2. Additional superannuation contributions - Payments above the standard superannuation guarantee made to an employee’s superannuation fund, whether they are employee/employer or pre-tax/post-tax contributions, can be added to an employee’s master record. These can then be automated through the payroll, e.g. salary sacrificed superannuation contributions. Endpoint documentation

post.description:
Creates a new department assignment for an employee. Commencement and Cease dates can be left as null to cover the employees hire date to their termination date. If an employee is changing departments, their previous department will need to be ceased the day before the new department commences NOTE: changing departments for dates that have already been calculated in a pay run may cause backpay Employees should always have a primary department, which you can do by setting isPrimary to true. You need to ensure there is only one primary department for any given date departmentId will need to determined from Department GET Endpoint documentation spitCostings allows you to have a principal (main costing, used from web and mobile drop downs) and other department costings for single costing, i.e. where costing is not split, splitCostings can be omitted. Example: 
{
    "departmentId": "075204e0-aab4-407f-8412-86940ee86cea",
    "isPrimary": true,
    "commencementDate": null,
    "ceaseDate": null,
    "splitCostings": [
    {
        "costingId": "075204e0-aab4-407f-8412-86940ee86cea",
        "splitPercentage": 100.0,
        "isPrincipal": true
    }]
}

sendInvitationEmail.description:
This field confirms whether a user invite is to be sent out. 
            
If the "primaryEmail" is provided, then you need to either choose to send out an invitation email or supply a password for the employee with the "newPassword" and "newConfirmPassword" fields.
            
NOTE: When SSO is enabled, and this is false, "newPassword" and "newConfirmPassword" must still be provided and must still match, but will be ignored.

primaryEmail.description:
This is the email address used as the employee's username.

Most commonly the employee's work email address is used, if applicable. If no email address is supplied then no user account will be created for the employee.

newPassword.description:
If applicable, the password to log into Definitiv can be set for the employee. 
            
If the "primaryEmail" is being sent, either "sendInvitationEmail" needs to be true or a value needs to be provided for this field.

newConfirmPassword.description:
If applicable, the password to log into Definitiv can be set for the employee.
            
If the "primaryEmail" is being sent, either "sendInvitationEmail" needs to be true or a value needs to be provided for this field.

customFields.description:
This section is only applicable if there are custom fields assigned to employee master records.
            
Custom fields do not need to be completed to add a new employee. However, if data for custom fields is being supplied, there is mandatory information that needs to be defined.

Definitiv.Api.Dtos.Employees.DepartmentA.description:
Represents a department assignment for an employee.
            
The DepartmentAssignmentDto class carries the details of a department assignment for an employee, 
such as assignment ID, department ID and name, primary department indicator, commencement and cease dates, as well as costing related details. 
It also includes a list of split costings for instances when the employee's costing is divided among multiple departments.
